one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed with Tower Insurance

I have been with Tower for quite a few years and had insurance with them for 3 cars and our house. I always thought I was with a good company, but after what happened with my car, I am honestly very disappointed.

In April, someone hit my car while it was parked. I was actually in hospital at the time. The police had my car towed to a yard, and when we found out, we went there and had to pay the towing fees.

I called Tower and explained everything. I asked if they could help with towing the car from the yard to my home because otherwise I would also have to keep paying the yard/storage fees. I was told they could not help with this. This was my first disappointment, and we had to arrange and pay another company to tow the car home ourselves.

I made a claim with Tower on the same day. I gave them the car registration details and the police report number. Because the accident was not my fault and I had Third Party Fire & Theft insurance, I expected Tower to help me with the claim.

They told me it might take some time. I waited and waited, and after around two and a half months I was told that the police had not given them enough information about the person who hit my car. I was then told they were going to close my claim because of the time limit, but that I could apply again.

I contacted the police myself and tried to sort everything out. The police even gave me another report which could help identify the other driver. I then applied for the claim again, as Tower told me to do.

But when I checked my Tower account online a few days later, I saw that my claim was already showing as closed. I didn’t even get a proper update from Tower before it was closed.

This is really frustrating. I paid over $300 for my insurance, and when I actually needed help after an accident that wasn’t my fault, I felt like I was left to deal with everything myself.

The panel beater has estimated around $6,000 to repair my car, so this is not a small matter for me.

I have been a loyal Tower customer with 3 car policies and 1 house policy, but after this experience I have completely lost trust in the company. I am now looking at moving my insurance to another company.

I understand that dealing with police reports and third-party information can take time, but I expected better communication and support from my insurance company.

Very disappointing experience after being a loyal customer for so many years. I just hope other people read reviews like this carefully before choosing their insurance company.
Wish if I could gave 0 star rating.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would give HK Kitchen zero stars if I could. My experience has been incredibly frustrating and disappointing.

There is damage to my kitchen, specifically in one corner around the cabinet/box area – nowhere near the tap or any plumbing. When I reported this, HK Kitchen immediately claimed it was caused by a water leak and refused to cover it under warranty.

This explanation simply doesn't make sense, and I have professional confirmation to prove it:

• I called a licensed plumber who thoroughly checked and confirmed there are no water leaks

• A specialist home inspector also confirmed no water leak exists and not sealed

• My insurance company had their own expert assess it, and they confirmed this is not water damage at all

Logically, if there were a genuine water leak, the damage would spread much further than just staying limited to that one isolated corner. It's clear this is simply poor workmanship that wasn't done properly in the first place.

Instead of standing behind their work, HK Kitchen has used a false "water damage" excuse to avoid their warranty obligations. I'm extremely disappointed with their service and their refusal to take responsibility.

I cannot recommend this company to anyone. They don't stand behind their work and will make up excuses to avoid fixing their mistakes. Save yourself the headache and money – go with a company that actually values its customers.

So we got an email saying that we owe $2400.00, Obviously we were flabbergasted as we had no sale, It seemed very wrong.
So after offering them a settlement figure and a notice of dismissal of services, they accepted our offer for $1900.00 which really hurt us financially.
After that we have spoken to heaps and heaps of people about that including other lawyers and lots of estate agents and every one said that was a ripoff BIGTIME.
And to top it off, Amber was so rude on two occasions, We will never use Innes Dean ever again.
Any one looking for a lawyer to do your transfer, there are heaps of lawyers who only charge if the sale is successful!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

My wife and I had a very negative and disappointing experience with Sorena Study Limited. We paid NZ$2,800 for immigration services in 2021, but after nearly five years of litigation, we were finally forced to go to the Disputes Tribunal of New Zealand to get our money back.

Importantly, the Tribunal officially ruled in our favor, stating that Sorena Study Limited had failed to provide evidence that they had provided the services they agreed to. Ultimately, the company was ordered to pay us NZ$2,924.

Based on our experience, I personally cannot recommend this company. I would suggest that any applicant thoroughly research the services, the qualifications of the consultants, the refund policy, and all promises made before paying any money, and keep everything in writing.
It's a shame they scheduled the meeting. We showed up on time, but they didn't come.

I would give Trident Home Kitchen zero stars if I could. Absolutely disgraceful service and zero accountability.

After they completed my kitchen, damage started appearing. When I contacted them about it under warranty, their response was beyond insulting – they actually blamed me for the damage, claiming it was caused by "mop cleaning."

This is completely absurd. I clean my kitchen the same way anyone would – there is nothing excessive or improper about normal mopping. A properly installed kitchen should be able to withstand basic cleaning without falling apart.

Instead of sending someone to properly assess and fix the issue, they've chosen the lazy, dishonest route: make up a ridiculous excuse about mopping and deny responsibility. It's obvious this is just poor workmanship and installation on their part.

Key issues:

• Shoddy installation that can't even handle normal cleaning

• Ridiculous warranty denial blaming the customer for mopping

• No willingness to inspect or properly assess the problem

• Zero customer care once they've been paid

A professional company would stand behind their work and ensure it's built to last. Trident Home Kitchen clearly cuts corners and then blames the homeowner when their poor quality shows.

Save your money and your sanity. Do not hire Trident Home Kitchen unless you want to be blamed for their incompetence.

Cannot recommend strongly enough to stay away.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am disappointed with the care I received from Dr Lee. I would like to apologise if any of my previous communication was unclear, as my intention was always to make sure I could continue receiving my medication and manage my medical needs properly.

I had concerns about the consistency of my medication dosage over time, as I was given different doses on several occasions. This caused confusion and concern for me, particularly because I experienced side effects that I felt were related to the dosage. I made it clear how badly I had been affected and how difficult the side effects were for me.

During my recent visit, I was advised to seek another doctor and was told to leave cause of my feedback I did before . I found this upsetting, especially because I was trying to honestly explain my concerns about my treatment and late payment was only 50$ smh . I was also worried about whether I would be able to continue receiving my medication.

I now have a new doctor, who has reviewed my medication and adjusted my dosage. I am currently back on the medication at a lower dose, including 5 mg and 500 mg of metformin, as prescribed by my new doctor. Since the change, I am no longer experiencing the itchiness I previously had. I am grateful that my new doctor listened to my concerns, reviewed the side effects I had experienced, and adjusted my treatment.

I would also like to sincerely apologise to the receptionist. I am sorry for any frustration or difficulty caused by the situation, including having to communicate with Dr Lee about my prescription. I understand that this may have been frustrating for you, and my apologies are directed to the receptionist only. I appreciate the help you provided.

My intention was never to cause problems for the staff. I simply wanted to be listened to, understand my medication properly, and make sure my medical needs were being managed safely and appropriately.

one_star_reviews.text:
We ordered takeout from this restaurant for the first time, and honestly, I don’t think I’ve ever been this disappointed with a takeaway.

The fried chicken was the worst fried chicken I’ve had in Auckland. It should have been called fried batter with a bit of chicken skin as there was barely any meat on it. The batter was tough, tasted awful, and was nothing like what you would expect from good fried chicken.

The chilli cheese fries were just as disappointing. The only thing that was actually edible was the chicken hoagie.

And the prices made the experience even worse:

Chicken hoagie – $25
Chilli cheese fries – $17
Fried chicken bowl – $22
Soft drink – $6

That’s $70 for a takeaway meal that was extremely poor quality. For those prices, I expected a lot more.

Honestly, we would have been better off ordering from KFC. At least we would have known what we were getting.

Extremely disappointing. Overpriced food with very poor quality. We will never order from here again. The fact that I’ve taken the time to write such a detailed review probably says more than anything about how disappointed I was with the experience.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience with this recruitment agency.

When I first contacted the agency, I was given the impression that there was a suitable job opportunity available and that, once my paperwork was completed and my CV had been reviewed and approved, the process would move forward quickly. I was also made to feel confident that the agency was genuinely interested in helping me secure employment.

Unfortunately, this has not been my experience. After completing the required paperwork and providing all the requested information, I have not seen the progress or communication that I was led to expect. The information and level of reassurance I received before signing up were very different from what happened afterwards.

I feel that I was given expectations that were not followed through, and this has left me feeling extremely disappointed and frustrated. As a client, I believe I deserve honest, transparent and professional communication throughout the recruitment process.

I hope the management of the agency takes my concerns seriously and reviews how clients are being treated and what information they are being given when they first sign up. People looking for work are placing their trust in recruitment agencies, and that trust should be respected.

I would appreciate a clear and honest explanation regarding my situation, including what happened with the job opportunity I was originally told about and whether there is still any genuine employment opportunity available.

I appreciate that grooming a Standard Poodle isn’t an easy job, but we were expecting a bit more care, attention to detail and transparency around the pricing. Sadly, the overall experience just wasn’t up to the standard we were hoping for.

A few weeks ago, I ordered a birthday cake from Penny Farthing Cakes, and unfortunately, the entire experience was extremely disappointing.

The cake was not ready at the agreed collection time, and the pickup was delayed more than once. This was a pre-ordered birthday cake for a special occasion, so the repeated delays were already frustrating.

When we finally received the cake, the flavour was not what we had originally discussed and agreed on, and the overall appearance was also disappointing and below our expectations.

However, the most concerning part was the hygiene and quality of the cake itself. We found pieces of eggshell inside the cake, and there was also a hair stuck to the cake. Unless hair is somehow part of the decoration, I really don’t understand how this passed the final check before being handed to a customer.

On top of that, the cake had a very strange taste, to the point that we did not feel comfortable continuing to eat it.

We placed this order weeks in advance and clearly discussed what we wanted. For a professionally made birthday cake, I expected much better quality, hygiene, communication and attention to detail.

Unfortunately, this was a very disappointing experience from beginning to end. I definitely will not be ordering from Penny Farthing Cakes again, and based on my personal experience, I cannot recommend them to anyone looking to order a cake for an important occasion.

I am honestly so disappointed with these NERO black cheer shoes.

The description says they are “Trialed and tested to go the distance” — unfortunately, the distance for us seems to be just 14 weeks.

My daughter wears these shoes twice a week for 1.5 hours each time, so around 3 hours a week. They have been worn indoors only and she has only worn them for one competition. After just 14 weeks, the sole has started coming away from the shoe.

I contacted the owner about this and was told it is “consistent with normal wear and use” and that, as a “gesture of goodwill”, they would offer me another pair at a discounted price of $90. I was also told to try Shoe Goo.

I honestly find this ridiculous. I paid $150 including shipping for these shoes, and I don't think having the sole come away after 14 weeks of light indoor use is acceptable quality for that price.

Unfortunately, the customer service has also been really disappointing. I expected the company to stand behind a product advertised as “trialed and tested to go the distance”, especially given how little use the shoes have actually had. Instead, I was essentially told this was normal wear and that I should repair them myself with Shoe Goo or buy another pair at a discounted price.

What disappoints me most is that the owner herself seems to consider this acceptable wear and tear. If this is the expected lifespan of the shoes, customers should be made aware that they may need replacing every few months.

I wouldn't purchase these again and, based on our experience, I would recommend looking at other companies.

one_star_reviews.text:
Since the car park operations was farmed off to a separate company, the ability to book online in advance for anything more than a day or two has disappeared.
You used to be able to book a week or two in any number of options (short/long/Orchard), but that is now gone "Sorry no availability for selected car park." for every search.
I am a frequent traveller, pre-booked 26 times in 2025, and 13 time so far in 2026 up until the end of June, then not one successful booking since then (not even park and ride shows as available).

Why does this matter? Because what use to cost less than $200 for a week to 10 days when pre-booked, is now above $300 through the gate. As most International flights land between midnight and 1am, nobody wants to wait around for infrequent shuttle buses in the cold/rain at that time to be carted off to the paddocks.

What used to be good when run by the Airport directly, is now very poor.

I’m sorry, but not sorry to say this — I will not be sending my son to Kaitaia College when his time comes.

From what I have personally seen, the school is dirty and at times feels more like a babysitting service than a place focused on education. If your child is already academic, independent and motivated, then they may do well. But if your child needs extra support, encouragement, structure or help understanding their learning, I would seriously question whether they are going to get what they need here.

There seems to be a real lack of structure, consistency and motivation within the school. Some teachers are great, but there are also far too many students being left to just get through the day rather than being inspired and supported to actually learn.

Our kids deserve better than that.

Definitely not an experience I would recommend.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m very disappointed with our experience at the Pre-Primary dance class this Saturday at point chev. The class was supposed to be taught by Ms Davis, but she was replaced by another teacher without any real notice.

I completely understand that teachers can sometimes be unavailable, but if a replacement is needed, I believe the school should choose someone who is genuinely engaged and enthusiastic about teaching young children.

Unfortunately, the replacement teacher appeared very uninterested and had very little interaction with the students. My daughter was sitting on the side instead of participating, and it was actually the assistant, Ms Nina, who made the effort to encourage her to join the class. This was particularly disappointing as it was the first time I’ve seen a teacher make so little effort to involve a child in the dance class.

I don’t think simply putting any replacement teacher in the class is enough. Parents are paying for a quality learning experience, and the children deserve a teacher who is patient, positive and genuinely wants to be there.

I really hope the school will reconsider how replacement teachers are arranged in the future and ensure that they are suitable and enthusiastic about working with young children

one_star_reviews.text:
Question: Do you honestly believe these conditions are acceptable?

We made the decision to uplift and transfer our loved one because of the conditions shown in the images below and the overall experience we had.

The cleanliness was horrendous. It was embarrassing to have family and friends come together to celebrate the life of our loved one in conditions like this. Upon arriving at the reception area, we were greeted by a rubbish skip bin, a run-down vehicle and rubbish scattered throughout the area.

In an industry where dignity, presentation and attention to detail should be of the highest importance, this was extremely disappointing. We were there throughout the day and, not once, did we see employees make any effort to pick up the rubbish or maintain the surroundings. Instead, staff walked past it and, in some cases, simply walked over it.

The level of service was also extremely disappointing. During our initial meeting, the funeral director excused herself to accept an Uber Eats delivery. Given the circumstances of our meeting, we found this incredibly inappropriate and disrespectful.

All I can say is: read the room. Is that truly appropriate when meeting with a grieving family who is there to make arrangements for the final farewell of their loved one?

We understand that times are difficult and that families can be under enormous emotional, mental and financial pressure when dealing with the loss of someone they love. However, that makes it even more important that families are treated with compassion, dignity, respect and professionalism.

Every family experiencing the loss of a loved one deserves better. They deserve to feel that their loved one is being cared for with the same dignity and respect that they would expect for their own family.

Our loved one deserved better. Our family deserved better. And quite honestly, we expected better.

I’m extremely disappointed with my experience with Cash Converters New Plymouth.

I won an auction for a device through their website, and the very next day I was informed that the auction had been cancelled because the device was supposedly faulty.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that there was no indication during the auction that the device had any issue. From my perspective, it is difficult not to question whether the auction was cancelled because the winning price was lower than they expected.

If an auction is advertised and a customer legitimately wins it, I believe the business should honour that transaction unless there is a genuine and verifiable reason why it cannot be fulfilled.

I expected much better from a well-known business. Unfortunately, this experience has left me feeling that the auction process cannot be trusted. Very disappointing.

I will be filing for tribunal why : I’m extremely disappointed with my experience with A2Z Cars.

I purchased my vehicle from them at the end of June 2026, and within approximately two months I have already experienced multiple problems and unexpected expenses.

The vehicle later failed a WOF inspection, with one rear tyre measured at only 1.4mm tread and the other at 1.7mm/borderline. I was advised that both tyres needed replacing and that a wheel alignment should be carried out because of the tyre wear. This cost me around $400.

A2Z Cars’ response is that the tyres were legal when the vehicle was sold because it had passed a WOF and that the deterioration is simply from me driving the vehicle. I understand that tyres are wear-and-tear items, but I seriously question how they reached this condition approximately two months after I bought the car, particularly when I was told the vehicle had been inspected before sale.

I have asked them to provide the actual tread-depth measurements from the time the vehicle was sold, rather than simply stating that the tyres were “legal.”

On top of this, the car has refused to start three separate times and has required jump-starting. I had the battery tested and it failed the battery health test. A2Z Cars has now told me that the auxiliary battery appears to be weak and would cost approximately $200 to replace, meaning I am expected to pay for another issue that has appeared only around two months after purchasing the vehicle.

The vehicle has also had a flashing check-engine light. A2Z Cars has offered to diagnose that issue, and I am giving them the opportunity to do so.

I purchased from a dealership because I expected a reasonable level of reliability and support. Instead, in approximately two months, I have dealt with two replacement tyres, a wheel alignment, repeated jump-starts, a failed battery health test and a flashing check-engine light.

I am very disappointed with how this has been handled. Based on my experience, I would not purchase another vehicle from A2Z Cars. I strongly recommend that anyone considering buying from them gets an independent pre-purchase inspection, including checking the exact tyre tread depths and battery health, regardless of whether the vehicle has a current WOF.

one_star_reviews.text:
I rented a Toyota Highlander from Speedy Rentals in August 2026. Unfortunately, the vehicle was involved in a minor rear-end accident during the rental period.

There were several aspects of my experience that I found very concerning.

Firstly, both drivers who drove the rental vehicle, Lin Wang and I, felt that the braking performance was not as good as we expected and that we needed to keep a longer following distance when driving. I cannot say whether there was a mechanical fault, as I have no independent mechanical report, but this was our experience while driving the vehicle.

After the accident, I paid Speedy Rentals the full NZ$3,500 excess stated in my rental agreement.

My main concern relates to the third-party liability cover. My rental agreement states that the rental includes third-party liability cover for liability arising from an incident up to NZ$15,000.

When I telephoned Speedy Rentals on Friday, 28 August to ask why the third-party damage was not being covered, the receptionist, Joanne, initially told me that “third-party damage” meant another vehicle damaging Speedy Rentals' car. After I explained my understanding of third-party liability insurance, I was then told that I had not purchased third-party insurance.

When I pointed out that my rental agreement expressly included third-party liability cover, the explanation changed again and I was told that the insurance did not apply because I had been driving carelessly.

Speedy Rentals subsequently confirmed to me in writing that the agreement does provide third-party liability cover up to $15,000, but said that they considered the cover void because of the careless-driving exclusion.

What concerns me further is that the third party's insurer, AA, separately wrote to me:

“We have been in contact with Speed rentals, they advised you did not take out insurance.”

This appears inconsistent with Speedy Rentals' later written acknowledgement to me that my rental agreement did provide third-party liability cover.

Regarding the accident circumstances, I had told Speedy that I looked at the GPS around the time of the accident. The cellphone was being used for navigation and was mounted in a phone holder supplied by Speedy Rentals with the rental vehicle. Speedy has relied on this to characterise my driving as careless and to say that all insurance cover was void. I do not agree that this should simply be determined by the rental company without the insurance position being properly assessed.

I have repeatedly asked Speedy Rentals to identify the insurer providing the third-party liability cover and to confirm whether an insurance claim has actually been lodged or formally declined.

AA has now told me that a claim needs to be lodged and that they are waiting for a claim number to cover the liability.

I am therefore extremely disappointed with the way the insurance issue has been handled. My concern is not that an accident occurred or that the rental vehicle was damaged—I accept those facts and have already paid the $3,500 excess. My concern is the conflicting explanations about the third-party insurance and the difficulty I have experienced trying to get the claim properly dealt with.

Based on my experience, I would recommend that anyone renting from Speedy Rentals carefully read and retain a copy of the rental agreement, particularly the insurance and exclusion clauses, and obtain clear written confirmation of exactly what third-party cover applies before driving away.

I hope Speedy Rentals will resolve this matter fairly and clarify the third-party insurance position.

I will update this review when Speedy Rentals provides its final response.

NEVER put a loved one into this facility. Gross negligence "un witnessed" falls, constipation that nothing was done for until 5 days later resulting in chronic stomach pain. Constipation was consistent. Scabies that was not treated in the correct manner. My mother was covered in dry itching skin. I contracted scabies from my mother the day she was dying as I lay with her. I went to my doctor 13 days after her passing to get treatment. When I presented my doctor letter to the regional manager she said "all this proves to me is that YOU had scabies"
They legally and negligently breached the EPOA of health order and NEVER consulted with the EPOA.
My mother was not offered end of life care because they said she wasn't in pain.....SHE WAS. I had to insist on it. The day she passed was recorded at 27 degrees. On dressing her her left shoulder was black and blue as well as chronic scabies (no record of how that happened, hence the pain she was in whenever I touched her shoulder) There was NO cooling either prior nor after death. No doctor to sign her off. The next day when the funeral director and I went to take her, I/we had to wait as no one had tended to cleaning her. And because of the heat her casket needed to be sealed immediately. I have a letter from the funeral director, he was appalled. I have since been in battle with bupa and loathe to pay 20k "outstanding" for what they DID NOT provide. Level of care is 3rd world. And BUPA MANAGEMENT TRULY DON'T CARE. Shame on you

Urgent: Please before making the decision to place a loved one here, read the factual report on the Health and Disability Commissioner (HDC) website. Our Dad paid the ultimate price for multiple breaches of care, as determined by an independent HDC investigation released 28 September 2026 (Case Reference: CAS-14310-J1D2D9). Should be zero stars.

One star for what they did well, sending the invoice for payment.

FACT: HDC made adverse comments about the GP.

FACT: HDC recommended both the facility and the GP provide a written letter of apology within a certain time frame. Both were one week late after yet another follow-up.

FACT: The owner, Belinda Brice has never apologised or fronted up in any form. According to their website, "Belinda is responsible for the continuing health of the Kumeu Village Families Business, ensuring our organisation's key objectives are met and our core philosophies are adhered to." Given the recent severe findings by the Health and Disability Commissioner, no words are needed, read the report before placing a loved one here.

Disgusting care,keep anyone you care about away from this dump.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would not recommend using this company. Based on my experience, and after reading similar reviews from others, I have concerns about the accuracy of their valuations, their turnaround times, and the professionalism of their service.

-Initial valuation experience
I had several jewellery items valued for insurance purposes. The valuation took two weeks longer than I had been advised, and the overall process did not appear professional.

-Concerns about undervaluation
After receiving the valuation, I read a number of reviews and noticed repeated comments suggesting that items had been undervalued. With this in mind, I took some of my jewellery to another valuation company. That second valuation confirmed my concerns: several items were valued between $500 and $2,000 higher than the original JVC valuation.

-Third-party valuation issue
I then decided to seek a third valuation to compare the results. What I did not know at the time was that this company outsourced its valuations to JVC Valuation Centre. When I went to collect the items and was told they were not ready, I realised they had been sent to JVC again.

This made the comparison particularly interesting. One ring came back valued another $1,000 lower than before. The explanation given was that the value of gold and diamonds had dropped. However, another item valued at the same time did not change in value, so that explanation did not seem consistent.

-Outcome
After explaining the situation to the company that had outsourced the valuation to JVC, I asked which valuation they considered more reliable. They advised that the other company’s valuation was more accurate. I have since continued using the other professional valuation company and NOT JVC. Overall, it appears that JVC Valuation Centre undervalued my jewellery by approximately $6,500.

I was able to change who I worked with but by that point I knew I couldn't say anything  bad about what they were and weren't doing, not that it would have mattered.  I was in NZ a full month before they even gave me the memo for employers, not that it was worth more than a blank sheet.  It was a full 6 months before they mentioned the accredited employer list.  None of the companies I had talked to had heard of this company so any claims that they have local knowledge and a good working relationship with local businesses is completely false.  Initially I was having to print out the forms, fill them out, scan and email them so they could fill them out online.  If you're having to fill out the forms and pay the processing fees why would you also pay someone several thousand dollars to just put that info into a webpage. one_star_reviews.text:
Coming from QLD, Australia and having years of rental experience there, I honestly found this agency so incredibly slow and unprofessional to deal with.

We had requests for maintenance when we moved in that took over 8 weeks to be rectified after numerous follow-up emails and messages. If we receive a response to this review, they will try and say they were waiting on the builders. But I sent emails for 5 weeks before Sophie rang me to ‘figure out what I was talking about’ before she then contacted the builders, and I do have emails to prove this. One issue still remains to this day…

When we decided to return to Australia and would be required to break our lease, I emailed Sophie first thing on a Friday morning, and it took Sophie until Monday at 3:45 pm before she had even forwarded our request to the owner for approval and acknowledged my email. There was no urgency for anything and no real professionalism we were used to in Australia. This could be the sheer lack of laws for tenants’ rights in NZ.

We understood there would be fees to pay when we ended up breaking our lease; however, these were supposed to be minimised by the agent. The advertised rent was higher than we were paying and higher than everything else for rent in the complex, which put us on the back foot from the start. An inspection was arranged for Monday. Sophie rang on the Tuesday to book another inspection in for Thursday as she only had one person turn up to the Monday inspection. We went out at the time for the inspection on the Thursday, and when we returned home, there was no card or evidence a viewing had occurred. I emailed Sophie to confirm the viewing had occurred and received an email back 24 hours later to advise that no, it hadn’t. But she hadn’t thought to let us know? If I hadn’t questioned this, I do wonder if we would have been charged for this inspection with our break lease fees.

Another inspection was booked for 12:00 pm the following Tuesday, to which Sophie turned up at 12:07 pm, which didn’t paint a good picture for potential tenants. Again, there was no feedback from Sophie, so I had to email to follow up on Thursday and then send a text message 24 hours later as no reply was received.

Then, despite giving four weeks’ notice, 1500 people viewing the listing AND every other property in the complex renting, Sophie could only find one tenant, and that tenant could not start until four weeks after we had vacated, meaning we were responsible for rent for four weeks plus break lease fees when we had given four weeks’ notice. We don’t feel our costs were minimised at all or that Sophie actively tried to find a new tenant for our property.

While I think Sophie did an excellent job of ensuring the owners were taken care of, I don’t feel, as a tenant, that our interests were ever a priority, and I don’t feel our costs were minimised during the exit process, which was very disappointing when we had tried our best to be good tenants and put up with constant delays for maintenance issues at the beginning of the tenancy.

We are now out more than our bond is worth for breaking the lease, and Sophie continues to insist this is a ‘lease break’ without considering we still have legal rights during this time as tenants.

Sophie also has no regard for her own personal morals as promised she would complete the exit inspection on Tuesday or Wednesday after I handed in the keys on Monday, and has now said she will not complete this until the end of the tenancy, which is in four weeks time, as she doesn’t like that I’ve questioned her on her methods. Given that we fly out of the country tomorrow, we will have no opportunity to sort out any issues now and have lost all our rights as tenants.

one_star_reviews.text:
"smart parking" only applies to those who benefit from ruining the day and place visited when using a car park they manage. I've always paid to park, but because of an oversite including waiting for lorries to clear access to/from a car park, and my wife taking time to enter the vehicle due to her osteoporosis, overshot the 'grace period' by a couple of minutes. This has cost me £60 on 2 occasions.
I accept I'm technically in the wrong, but there is no tolerance for being "in" the car park longer than the time paid for, despite not actually being in a space.
I advise anyone either to not use their managed car parks or if they do, run to the ticket machine as quickly as possible because the clock has started ticking!
